approximation_gap : ∀ (ε : Real),
  Real.instLT.lt 0 ε →
    Real.instLE.le ε 1 →
      ∀ (f t c : Nat),
        Real.instLE.le 1
            (instHMul.hMul c.cast (instHSub.hSub (instHMul.hMul t.cast ε) (instHMul.hMul f.cast (instHSub.hSub 1 ε)))) →
          ∀ (m : Nat),
            Real.instLT.lt
              (instHMul.hMul
                ((Lax323828.SamplingParameters.vertexBound f t (Lax323828.SamplingParameters.repetitions c m)
                        m).cast.rpow
                  (instHSub.hSub 1 ε))
                (Lax323828.SamplingParameters.threshold m).cast)
              (Lax323828.SamplingParameters.sampleCount t (Lax323828.SamplingParameters.repetitions c m) m).cast

choose_multiplier : ∀ (ε : Real) (f t : Nat),
  Real.instLT.lt 0 (instHSub.hSub (instHMul.hMul t.cast ε) (instHMul.hMul f.cast (instHSub.hSub 1 ε))) →
    Exists fun c =>
      And (instLTNat.lt 0 c)
        (Real.instLE.le 1
          (instHMul.hMul c.cast (instHSub.hSub (instHMul.hMul t.cast ε) (instHMul.hMul f.cast (instHSub.hSub 1 ε)))))

polynomial_bound : ∀ (f t c m : Nat),
  instLENat.le (Lax323828.SamplingParameters.vertexBound f t (Lax323828.SamplingParameters.repetitions c m) m)
    (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow 16 (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd t f) c))
      (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd m 2) (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd t f) c) 1)))

concepts.title: The averaged table preserves the answers of an accepting side-condition test
concepts.description:
Let $U$ be the words satisfying the side condition $h$. If the extended
CNA test accepts a table $A$, then averaging its sign-valued version over
coordinates outside $U$ preserves every base query answer of that run.
Indeed, step (3) requires the table to have the same answer on every
function agreeing with the query on $U$.

This links the actual test definition to the averaged function in equation
(17) and to its Fourier projection formula, Lemma 4.18.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.LongCode
import Lax323828.FourierProjection

/-!
---
title: The averaged table preserves the answers of an accepting side-condition test
type: theorem
---
Let $U$ be the words satisfying the side condition $h$. If the extended
CNA test accepts a table $A$, then averaging its sign-valued version over
coordinates outside $U$ preserves every base query answer of that run.
Indeed, step (3) requires the table to have the same answer on every
function agreeing with the query on $U$.

This links the actual test definition to the averaged function in equation
(17) and to its Fourier projection formula, Lemma 4.18.
-/

namespace Lax323828.SideConditionAveraging

open LongCode BooleanFourier FourierProjection

def satisfying {w : ℕ} (h : Coordinate w) : Finset (Word w) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun x ↦ h x = true

axiom query_preserved {w s : ℕ} (A : Table w) (f : Fin s → Coordinate w)
    (h : Coordinate w) (hpass : AcceptsWithCondition A f h)
    (g : Coordinate w) (hg : Queried f g) :
  project (fun q ↦ sign (A q)) (satisfying h) g = sign (A g)

end Lax323828.SideConditionAveraging

statements.signature:
query_preserved : ∀ {w s : Nat} (A : Lax323828.LongCode.Table w) (f : Fin s → Lax323828.LongCode.Coordinate w)
  (h : Lax323828.LongCode.Coordinate w),
  Lax323828.LongCode.AcceptsWithCondition A f h →
    ∀ (g : Lax323828.LongCode.Coordinate w),
      Lax323828.LongCode.Queried f g →
        Eq
          (Lax323828.FourierProjection.project (fun q => Lax323828.BooleanFourier.sign (A q))
            (Lax323828.SideConditionAveraging.satisfying h) g)
          (Lax323828.BooleanFourier.sign (A g))

concepts.title: Higher-moment bound for the small-coefficient CNA term
concepts.description:
For coefficients of degree at most $\ell$, squared mass at most one,
and absolute value at most $\delta$, split the mixed-moment expansion
according to the union size of its double covers. Small unions contribute
the bounds from Lemma 4.16; unions of size at least $r$ contribute at
most the total double-cover weight times the mixed-correlation bound.
This gives the normalized higher-moment estimate underlying Lemma 4.10
and, for even moments, its probability bound.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.HighDegreeSoundness
import Lax323828.SmallUnionDoubleCovers
import Lax323828.MixedPredicateMoments

/-!
---
title: Higher-moment bound for the small-coefficient CNA term
type: theorem
---
For coefficients of degree at most $\ell$, squared mass at most one,
and absolute value at most $\delta$, split the mixed-moment expansion
according to the union size of its double covers. Small unions contribute
the bounds from Lemma 4.16; unions of size at least $r$ contribute at
most the total double-cover weight times the mixed-correlation bound.
This gives the normalized higher-moment estimate underlying Lemma 4.10
and, for even moments, its probability bound.
-/

namespace Lax323828.SmallCoefficientSoundness

open HighDegreeSoundness FiniteProbability
open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable def boundValue (l m r N : ℕ) (δ q : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ t ∈ Finset.range r, (2 : ℝ) ^ m * ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * δ) ^ (m - 2 * t) *
    (1 + (3 : ℝ) ^ (l * (4 * t + 1) * 2 ^ (2 * t)))) +
  (1 + (3 : ℝ) ^ (l * (2 * m + 1) * 2 ^ m)) *
    (q ^ r + (2 : ℝ) ^ m * (2 * (N + 1 : ℝ) * Real.exp (-(N : ℝ) * q ^ 2 / 2)))

axiom moment_bound {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hN : Fintype.card κ = 2 * n)
    (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (l m r : ℕ) (δ q : ℝ)
    (hsmall : ∀ S, |c S| ≤ δ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1)
    (hdegree : ∀ S, l < S.card → c S = 0) (henergy : ∑ S, c S ^ 2 ≤ 1)
    (hr : 2 * r ≤ m) :
  (𝔼 f : ι → κ, normalizedSum Finset.univ c n f ^ m) ≤
    boundValue l m r (Fintype.card κ) δ q

axiom tail_bound {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hN : Fintype.card κ = 2 * n)
    (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (l m r : ℕ) (δ q : ℝ)
    (hsmall : ∀ S, |c S| ≤ δ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1)
    (hdegree : ∀ S, l < S.card → c S = 0) (henergy : ∑ S, c S ^ 2 ≤ 1)
    (hr : 2 * r ≤ m) (hm : Even m) (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
  probability (fun f : ι → κ ↦ a ≤ normalizedSum Finset.univ c n f) ≤
    boundValue l m r (Fintype.card κ) δ q / a ^ m

end Lax323828.SmallCoefficientSoundness

moment_bound : ∀ {ι κ : Type} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_2 : Fintype κ] [inst_3 : DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ]
  (n : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    Eq (Fintype.card κ) (instHMul.hMul 2 n) →
      ∀ (c : Finset ι → Real) (l m r : Nat) (δ q : Real),
        (∀ (S : Finset ι), Real.instLE.le (abs (c S)) δ) →
          Real.instLE.le 0 δ →
            Real.instLE.le 0 q →
              Real.instLE.le q 1 →
                (∀ (S : Finset ι), instLTNat.lt l S.card → Eq (c S) 0) →
                  Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun S => instHPow.hPow (c S) 2) 1 →
                    instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 2 r) m →
                      Real.instLE.le
                        (Finset.univ.expect fun f =>
                          instHPow.hPow (Lax323828.HighDegreeSoundness.normalizedSum Finset.univ c n f) m)
                        (Lax323828.SmallCoefficientSoundness.boundValue l m r (Fintype.card κ) δ q)

tail_bound : ∀ {ι κ : Type} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_2 : Fintype κ] [inst_3 : DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ]
  (n : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    Eq (Fintype.card κ) (instHMul.hMul 2 n) →
      ∀ (c : Finset ι → Real) (l m r : Nat) (δ q : Real),
        (∀ (S : Finset ι), Real.instLE.le (abs (c S)) δ) →
          Real.instLE.le 0 δ →
            Real.instLE.le 0 q →
              Real.instLE.le q 1 →
                (∀ (S : Finset ι), instLTNat.lt l S.card → Eq (c S) 0) →
                  Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun S => instHPow.hPow (c S) 2) 1 →
                    instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 2 r) m →
                      Even m →
                        ∀ (a : Real),
                          Real.instLT.lt 0 a →
                            Real.instLE.le
                              (Lax323828.FiniteProbability.probability fun f =>
                                Real.instLE.le a (Lax323828.HighDegreeSoundness.normalizedSum Finset.univ c n f))
                              (instHDiv.hDiv (Lax323828.SmallCoefficientSoundness.boundValue l m r (Fintype.card κ) δ q)
                                (instHPow.hPow a m))

concepts.title: The size of the decoding set from large coefficients
concepts.description:
Let real coefficients $c_\alpha$ be indexed by subsets of an $n$-element
set and satisfy $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha^2\leq1$. For $\delta>0$, take the
union $S$ of the sets $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\leq\ell$ and
$c_\alpha^2\geq\ell\delta$. Then $|S|\leq1/\delta$.

This is the counting argument for the decoding set in equation (2) of
Håstad's paper. Applied to Fourier coefficients using Parseval's identity
and $\delta=2^{-\varepsilon s}$, it gives $|S|\leq2^{\varepsilon s}$.
The statement below isolates the counting argument; its energy bound is an
explicit hypothesis, not an assumed Fourier identity.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset

/-!
---
title: The size of the decoding set from large coefficients
type: theorem
---
Let real coefficients $c_\alpha$ be indexed by subsets of an $n$-element
set and satisfy $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha^2\leq1$. For $\delta>0$, take the
union $S$ of the sets $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\leq\ell$ and
$c_\alpha^2\geq\ell\delta$. Then $|S|\leq1/\delta$.

This is the counting argument for the decoding set in equation (2) of
Håstad's paper. Applied to Fourier coefficients using Parseval's identity
and $\delta=2^{-\varepsilon s}$, it gives $|S|\leq2^{\varepsilon s}$.
The statement below isolates the counting argument; its energy bound is an
explicit hypothesis, not an assumed Fourier identity.
-/

namespace Lax323828.SmallSupport

open scoped Classical

/-- The coordinate sets of size at most `l` whose squared coefficient is at least `l * δ`. -/
noncomputable def largeSets {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (l : ℕ)
    (δ : ℝ) : Finset (Finset ι) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun a ↦ a.card ≤ l ∧ (l : ℝ) * δ ≤ c a ^ 2

/-- The union of the coordinate sets selected by `largeSets`. -/
noncomputable def decodingSet {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (l : ℕ)
    (δ : ℝ) : Finset ι :=
  (largeSets c l δ).biUnion id

axiom decodingSet_bound {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (l : ℕ)
    (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (henergy : ∑ a, c a ^ 2 ≤ 1) :
  ((decodingSet c l δ).card : ℝ) ≤ 1 / δ

end Lax323828.SmallSupport

  Real.instLT.lt 0 δ →
    Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun a => instHPow.hPow (c a) 2) 1 →
      Real.instLE.le (Lax323828.SmallSupport.decodingSet c l δ).card.cast (instHDiv.hDiv 1 δ)

concepts.title: Small-union weighted double-cover estimate
concepts.description:
If every coefficient is at most $\delta$, double covers of a set of size
$t$ have total weight at most a dimension-independent constant times
$\delta^{m-2t}$. This is the estimate in Lemma 4.16. Extract $2t$
positions that still cover every point twice. Each remaining support is
one of at most $2^t$ subsets of their union.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.DoubleCoverBounds

/-!
---
title: Small-union weighted double-cover estimate
type: theorem
---
If every coefficient is at most $\delta$, double covers of a set of size
$t$ have total weight at most a dimension-independent constant times
$\delta^{m-2t}$. This is the estimate in Lemma 4.16. Extract $2t$
positions that still cover every point twice. Each remaining support is
one of at most $2^t$ subsets of their union.
-/

namespace Lax323828.SmallUnionDoubleCovers

open scoped Classical

open HigherMoments
open scoped BigOperators

/-- The total product weight of double-cover tuples whose union has exactly `t` coordinates. -/
noncomputable def weight {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (m t : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ S : Fin m → Finset ι,
    if DoubleCover S ∧ (Finset.univ.biUnion S).card = t then ∏ j, c (S j) else 0

axiom bound {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (c : Finset ι → ℝ) (l m t : ℕ) (δ : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ S, 0 ≤ c S) (hsmall : ∀ S, c S ≤ δ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hdegree : ∀ S, l < S.card → c S = 0) (henergy : ∑ S, c S ^ 2 ≤ 1)
    (hmt : 2 * t ≤ m) :
  weight c m t ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ m * ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * δ) ^ (m - 2 * t) *
    (1 + (3 : ℝ) ^ (l * (4 * t + 1) * 2 ^ (2 * t)))

end Lax323828.SmallUnionDoubleCovers

statements.signature:
bound : ∀ {ι : Type} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] (c : Finset ι → Real) (l m t : Nat) (δ : Real),
  (∀ (S : Finset ι), Real.instLE.le 0 (c S)) →
    (∀ (S : Finset ι), Real.instLE.le (c S) δ) →
      Real.instLE.le 0 δ →
        (∀ (S : Finset ι), instLTNat.lt l S.card → Eq (c S) 0) →
          Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun S => instHPow.hPow (c S) 2) 1 →
            instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 2 t) m →
              Real.instLE.le (Lax323828.SmallUnionDoubleCovers.weight c m t)
                (instHMul.hMul
                  (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow 2 m)
                    (instHPow.hPow (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow 2 t) δ) (instHSub.hSub m (instHMul.hMul 2 t))))
                  (instHAdd.hAdd 1
                    (instHPow.hPow 3
                      (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul l (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 4 t) 1))
                        (instHPow.hPow 2 (instHMul.hMul 2 t))))))

concepts.title: Small-value projection games for every registered NP language
concepts.description:
Every language in the registered certificate definition of NP has a
polynomial-size reduction to projection games of arbitrarily small positive
value. The answer alphabets depend only on the target value. The polynomial
bound can depend on the language. Completeness is perfect.

The proof connects the registered stack-machine verifiers to Cook–Levin,
then applies the proved finite gap and fortification construction. This
statement records semantic correctness and size; the machine implementation

import Lax323828.SmallValueSatisfiability
import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Small-value projection games for every registered NP language
type: theorem
---
Every language in the registered certificate definition of NP has a
polynomial-size reduction to projection games of arbitrarily small positive
value. The answer alphabets depend only on the target value. The polynomial
bound can depend on the language. Completeness is perfect.

The proof connects the registered stack-machine verifiers to Cook–Levin,
then applies the proved finite gap and fortification construction. This
statement records semantic correctness and size; the machine implementation
of the complete game transformation is a separate obligation.
-/

namespace Lax323828.SmallValueNP

open CenteredProjection

axiom reduction (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ x y : ℕ, 0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧
      ∀ L ∈ Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP, ∃ K e : ℕ,
        ∀ z : List Bool,
          ∃ u o w : ℕ, 0 < u ∧ 0 < o ∧ 0 < w ∧ u + o + w ≤ K * (z.length + 1) ^ e ∧
            ∃ G : System (Fin u) (Fin o) (Fin w) (Fin x) (Fin y),
              (z ∈ L → G.Complete) ∧ (z ∉ L → G.Sound δ)

end Lax323828.SmallValueNP

  Real.instLT.lt 0 δ →
    Exists fun x =>
      Exists fun y =>
        And (instLTNat.lt 0 x)
          (And (instLTNat.lt 0 y)
            (∀ (L : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Language),
              Set.instMembership.mem Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP L →
                Exists fun K =>
                  Exists fun e =>
                    ∀ (z : List Bool),
                      Exists fun u =>
                        Exists fun o =>
                          Exists fun w =>
                            And (instLTNat.lt 0 u)
                              (And (instLTNat.lt 0 o)
                                (And (instLTNat.lt 0 w)
                                  (And
                                    (instLENat.le (instHAdd.hAdd (instHAdd.hAdd u o) w)
                                      (instHMul.hMul K (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd z.length 1) e)))
                                    (Exists fun G =>
                                      And (Set.instMembership.mem L z → G.Complete)
                                        (Not (Set.instMembership.mem L z) → G.Sound δ)))))))

concepts.title: A polynomial-size 3-SAT reduction to arbitrarily small projection-game value
concepts.description:
For every fixed positive soundness δ, exact 3-CNF formulas reduce to centered
projection games over fixed answer alphabets. Satisfiable formulas give
perfectly complete games, and unsatisfiable formulas give value at most δ.
The sum of all three question-space sizes is bounded by one fixed polynomial
in the number of clauses.

This combines the regular Dinur gap, projection symmetrization, tuple
fortification, repeated squaring, and Cauchy–Schwarz. It is a finite
mathematical reduction; the uniform machine running-time proof is separate.

-/

open CenteredProjection GapSatisfiability

axiom reduction (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ x y K e : ℕ, 0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧
      ∀ φ : Formula, Is3CNF φ →
        ∃ u o w : ℕ, 0 < u ∧ 0 < o ∧ 0 < w ∧ u + o + w ≤ K * (φ.length + 1) ^ e ∧
          ∃ G : System (Fin u) (Fin o) (Fin w) (Fin x) (Fin y),
            (Satisfiable φ → G.Complete) ∧ (¬ Satisfiable φ → G.Sound δ)

end Lax323828.SmallValueSatisfiability

concepts.title: Repetition of local proof tests
concepts.description:
Repeat a verifier $k$ times against the same global proof and accept only
when every run accepts. Accepting local views are unions of compatible
base views. The acceptance probability of each fixed proof is raised to
the $k$th power, and $A$ base accepting views give at most $A^k$ repeated
views per random choice. Perfect completeness is preserved.

This is repetition of a one-oracle PCP verifier. It is distinct from the
two-prover parallel-repetition theorem, whose strategies may depend on
entire question tuples.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.TestSampling
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin

/-!
---
title: Repetition of local proof tests
type: theorem
---
Repeat a verifier $k$ times against the same global proof and accept only
when every run accepts. Accepting local views are unions of compatible
base views. The acceptance probability of each fixed proof is raised to
the $k$th power, and $A$ base accepting views give at most $A^k$ repeated
views per random choice. Perfect completeness is preserved.

This is repetition of a one-oracle PCP verifier. It is distinct from the
two-prover parallel-repetition theorem, whose strategies may depend on
entire question tuples.
-/

namespace Lax323828.TestRepetition

open scoped Classical

open LocalTests TestSampling FiniteProbability

/-- Every pair of local views gives the same answer wherever both are defined. -/
def Coherent {m k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → View m) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, Compatible (a i) (a j)

/-- Combine the views into one partial assignment, using the first available answer at each coordinate. -/
def merge {m : ℕ} : {k : ℕ} → (Fin k → View m) → View m
  | 0, _ => fun _ ↦ none
  | k + 1, a => fun i ↦ (a 0 i).or (merge (fun j : Fin k ↦ a j.succ) i)

/-- Number the `r^k` sequences of `k` random choices using their base-`r` digits. -/
def seedEquiv (r k : ℕ) : (Fin k → Fin r) ≃ Fin (r ^ k) :=
  finFunctionFinEquiv

/-- Keep every coherent combination of accepting views from the `k` runs, and merge each combination. -/
noncomputable def repeated {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (k : ℕ) : System (r ^ k) m :=
  ⟨fun z ↦ ((Fintype.piFinset (fun i : Fin k ↦ C.accepting ((seedEquiv r k).symm z i))).filter
    Coherent).image merge⟩

axiom passes_iff {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (k : ℕ) (π : Oracle m) (z : Fin (r ^ k)) :
  Passes (repeated C k) π z ↔ ∀ i, Passes C π ((seedEquiv r k).symm z i)

axiom acceptance_probability {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (k : ℕ) (π : Oracle m) :
  probability (Passes (repeated C k) π) = probability (Passes C π) ^ k

axiom free_bits {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (k A : ℕ)
    (hA : ∀ z, (C.accepting z).card ≤ A) :
  ∀ z, ((repeated C k).accepting z).card ≤ A ^ k

axiom perfect_completeness {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (k : ℕ) (hC : Complete C) :
  Complete (repeated C k)

axiom soundness {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (k : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 ≤ p)
    (hC : Sound C p) : Sound (repeated C k) (p ^ k)

end Lax323828.TestRepetition

  Eq (Lax323828.FiniteProbability.probability (Lax323828.TestSampling.Passes (Lax323828.TestRepetition.repeated C k) π))
    (instHPow.hPow (Lax323828.FiniteProbability.probability (Lax323828.TestSampling.Passes C π)) k)

    ∀ (z : Fin (instHPow.hPow r k)),
      instLENat.le ((Lax323828.TestRepetition.repeated C k).accepting z).card (instHPow.hPow A k)

    (∀ (i : Fin k),
      Lax323828.TestSampling.Passes C π (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe (Lax323828.TestRepetition.seedEquiv r k).symm z i))

  Lax323828.TestSampling.Complete C → Lax323828.TestSampling.Complete (Lax323828.TestRepetition.repeated C k)

  Real.instLE.le 0 p →
    Lax323828.TestSampling.Sound C p →
      Lax323828.TestSampling.Sound (Lax323828.TestRepetition.repeated C k) (instHPow.hPow p k)

concepts.title: Random sparsification of a consistency graph
concepts.description:
Sample $N$ independent random choices of a finite local-test system, with
replacement, and construct its consistency graph. Every sampled choice
keeps its own index, including repeated choices. Perfect completeness is
preserved for every sample, and $A$ accepting views per choice give at most
$NA$ vertices.

If every proof is accepted with probability at most $p$ and $Np\geq m+2$,
where $m$ is the proof length, then with probability at least $3/4$ the
sampled graph has clique number less than $4Np$. The bound holds
simultaneously for every proof, including proofs chosen after sampling.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.LocalTests
import Lax323828.EncodedReduction
import Lax323828.BernoulliSampling

/-!
---
title: Random sparsification of a consistency graph
type: theorem
---
Sample $N$ independent random choices of a finite local-test system, with
replacement, and construct its consistency graph. Every sampled choice
keeps its own index, including repeated choices. Perfect completeness is
preserved for every sample, and $A$ accepting views per choice give at most
$NA$ vertices.

If every proof is accepted with probability at most $p$ and $Np\geq m+2$,
where $m$ is the proof length, then with probability at least $3/4$ the
sampled graph has clique number less than $4Np$. The bound holds
simultaneously for every proof, including proofs chosen after sampling.
-/

namespace Lax323828.TestSampling

open LocalTests FiniteProbability ConsistencyGraph

def Passes {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (π : Oracle m) (seed : Fin r) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ C.accepting seed, Extends π a

def Complete {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) : Prop := ∃ π, ∀ seed, Passes C π seed

def Sound {r m : ℕ} (C : System r m) (p : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ π, probability (Passes C π) ≤ p

def sampled {r m N : ℕ} (C : System r m) (z : Fin N → Fin r) : System N m :=
  ⟨fun i ↦ C.accepting (z i)⟩

axiom vertex_bound {r m N : ℕ} (C : System r m) (z : Fin N → Fin r)
    (A : ℕ) (hA : ∀ seed, (C.accepting seed).card ≤ A) :
    Fintype.card (Vertex (sampled C z)) ≤ N * A

axiom perfect_completeness {r m N : ℕ} (C : System r m) (hC : Complete C)
    (z : Fin N → Fin r) :
    (EncodedReduction.output (sampled C z)).cliqueNumber = N

axiom soundness {r m N : ℕ} (hr : 0 < r) (C : System r m) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 ≤ p)
    (hC : Sound C p) (hN : (m : ℝ) + 2 ≤ N * p) :
    probability (fun z : Fin N → Fin r ↦
      4 * N * p ≤ ((EncodedReduction.output (sampled C z)).cliqueNumber : ℝ)) ≤ 1 / 4

end Lax323828.TestSampling

concepts.title: Dimension-independent bounds for tuple averaging
concepts.description:
The average of t independent samples of a function in [-1,1] has variance
at most 1/t. Restricting to any event cannot increase its unnormalized
correlation with the centered sample average beyond 1/sqrt(t).
These bounds do not depend on the size of the sample alphabet. They provide
the averaging estimate for fortifying projection games by tuple questions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.FiniteProbability
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi

/-!
---
title: Dimension-independent bounds for tuple averaging
type: theorem
---
The average of t independent samples of a function in [-1,1] has variance
at most 1/t. Restricting to any event cannot increase its unnormalized
correlation with the centered sample average beyond 1/sqrt(t).
These bounds do not depend on the size of the sample alphabet. They provide
the averaging estimate for fortifying projection games by tuple questions.
-/

namespace Lax323828.TupleAveraging

open scoped BigOperators

axiom variance_bound {A : Type} [Fintype A] [Nonempty A]
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (f : A → ℝ) (hf : ∀ a, |f a| ≤ 1) :
    (𝔼 z : Fin t → A, ((𝔼 i, f (z i)) - (𝔼 a, f a)) ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (t : ℝ)

axiom restriction_correlation {A : Type} [Fintype A] [Nonempty A]
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (f : A → ℝ) (hf : ∀ a, |f a| ≤ 1)
    (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) [DecidablePred S] :
    |𝔼 z : Fin t → A, if S z then (𝔼 i, f (z i)) - (𝔼 a, f a) else 0| ^ 2 ≤
      1 / (t : ℝ)

end Lax323828.TupleAveraging

statements.signature:
restriction_correlation : ∀ {A : Type} [inst : Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 t →
    ∀ (f : A → Real),
      (∀ (a : A), Real.instLE.le (abs (f a)) 1) →
        ∀ (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) [inst_2 : DecidablePred S],
          Real.instLE.le
            (instHPow.hPow
              (abs
                (Finset.univ.expect fun z =>
                  ite (S z) (instHSub.hSub (Finset.univ.expect fun i => f (z i)) (Finset.univ.expect fun a => f a)) 0))
              2)
            (instHDiv.hDiv 1 t.cast)

variance_bound : ∀ {A : Type} [inst : Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 t →
    ∀ (f : A → Real),
      (∀ (a : A), Real.instLE.le (abs (f a)) 1) →
        Real.instLE.le
          (Finset.univ.expect fun z =>
            instHPow.hPow (instHSub.hSub (Finset.univ.expect fun i => f (z i)) (Finset.univ.expect fun a => f a)) 2)
          (instHDiv.hDiv 1 t.cast)

concepts.title: Fortification by uniformly sampled tuples
concepts.description:
Replace each prover question by a uniform tuple with the original question
planted at a hidden uniformly chosen coordinate, and ask the prover to
answer every coordinate. This preserves perfect completeness, soundness,
and uniform question marginals. For tuple length t, the resulting game is
fortified with additive error at most 4r whenever 1/t ≤ r².

The construction uses all tuples. Its size is polynomial in the original
question count for each fixed t; its mixing bound is independent of the
prover-answer alphabet.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.FortifiedSquaring
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi

/-!
---
title: Fortification by uniformly sampled tuples
type: theorem
---
Replace each prover question by a uniform tuple with the original question
planted at a hidden uniformly chosen coordinate, and ask the prover to
answer every coordinate. This preserves perfect completeness, soundness,
and uniform question marginals. For tuple length t, the resulting game is
fortified with additive error at most 4r whenever 1/t ≤ r².

The construction uses all tuples. Its size is polynomial in the original
question count for each fixed t; its mixing bound is independent of the
prover-answer alphabet.
-/

namespace Lax323828.TupleFortification

open FortifiedSquaring
open scoped BigOperators

abbrev History (t : ℕ) (W : Type) := Fin t × (Fin t → W)

def plant {W : Type} {t : ℕ} (w : W) (h : History t W) : Fin t → W :=
  Function.update h.2 h.1 w

def lift {Z W A B : Type} (G : Game Z W A B) (t : ℕ) :
    Game (Z × (History t W × History t W)) (Fin t → W) (Fin t → A) B where
  left z := plant (G.left z.1) z.2.1
  right z := plant (G.right z.1) z.2.2
  validLeft z a := G.validLeft z.1 (a z.2.1.1)
  validRight z b := G.validRight z.1 (b z.2.2.1)
  projectLeft z a := G.projectLeft z.1 (a z.2.1.1)
  projectRight z b := G.projectRight z.1 (b z.2.2.1)

axiom soundness {Z W A B : Type} [Fintype Z] [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W]
    [Nonempty W] [Fintype A] (G : Game Z W A B) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (s : ℝ) (hG : G.Sound s) : (lift G t).Sound s

axiom fortification {Z W A B : Type}
    [Fintype Z] [Nonempty Z] [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] [Nonempty W]
    [Fintype A] [Nonempty A]
    (G : Game Z W A B)
    (hl : ∀ f : W → ℝ, (𝔼 z, f (G.left z)) = (𝔼 w, f w))
    (hr : ∀ f : W → ℝ, (𝔼 z, f (G.right z)) = (𝔼 w, f w))
    (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hs1 : s ≤ 1) (hG : G.Sound s)
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (htr : 1 / (t : ℝ) ≤ r ^ 2) :
    (lift G t).Fortified s (4 * r)

axiom left_uniform {Z W A B : Type} [Fintype Z] [Fintype W] [Nonempty W]
    (G : Game Z W A B)
    (hl : ∀ f : W → ℝ, (𝔼 z, f (G.left z)) = (𝔼 w, f w))
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (f : (Fin t → W) → ℝ) :
    (𝔼 z, f ((lift G t).left z)) = 𝔼 w, f w

axiom right_uniform {Z W A B : Type} [Fintype Z] [Fintype W] [Nonempty W]
    (G : Game Z W A B)
    (hr : ∀ f : W → ℝ, (𝔼 z, f (G.right z)) = (𝔼 w, f w))
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (f : (Fin t → W) → ℝ) :
    (𝔼 z, f ((lift G t).right z)) = 𝔼 w, f w

axiom completeness {Z W A B : Type} (G : Game Z W A B)
    (P Q : W → A) (h : ∀ z, G.Wins P Q z) (t : ℕ) :
    ∀ z, (lift G t).Wins (fun w i ↦ P (w i)) (fun w i ↦ Q (w i)) z

end Lax323828.TupleFortification

completeness : ∀ {Z W A B : Type} (G : Lax323828.FortifiedSquaring.Game Z W A B) (P Q : W → A),
  (∀ (z : Z), G.Wins P Q z) →
    ∀ (t : Nat)
      (z : Prod Z (Prod (Lax323828.TupleFortification.History t W) (Lax323828.TupleFortification.History t W))),
      (Lax323828.TupleFortification.lift G t).Wins (fun w i => P (w i)) (fun w i => Q (w i)) z

  [Nonempty A] (G : Lax323828.FortifiedSquaring.Game Z W A B),
  (∀ (f : W → Real), Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun z => f (G.left z)) (Finset.univ.expect fun w => f w)) →
    (∀ (f : W → Real), Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun z => f (G.right z)) (Finset.univ.expect fun w => f w)) →
      ∀ (s : Real),
        Real.instLE.le 0 s →
          Real.instLE.le s 1 →
            G.Sound s →
              ∀ (t : Nat),
                instLTNat.lt 0 t →
                  ∀ (r : Real),
                    Real.instLE.le 0 r →
                      Real.instLE.le (instHDiv.hDiv 1 t.cast) (instHPow.hPow r 2) →
                        (Lax323828.TupleFortification.lift G t).Fortified s (instHMul.hMul 4 r)

  (∀ (f : W → Real), Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun z => f (G.left z)) (Finset.univ.expect fun w => f w)) →
    ∀ (t : Nat),
      instLTNat.lt 0 t →
        ∀ (f : (Fin t → W) → Real),
          Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun z => f ((Lax323828.TupleFortification.lift G t).left z))
            (Finset.univ.expect fun w => f w)

right_uniform : ∀ {Z W A B : Type} [inst : Fintype Z] [inst_1 : Fintype W] [Nonempty W] (G : Lax323828.FortifiedSquaring.Game Z W A B),
  (∀ (f : W → Real), Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun z => f (G.right z)) (Finset.univ.expect fun w => f w)) →
    ∀ (t : Nat),
      instLTNat.lt 0 t →
        ∀ (f : (Fin t → W) → Real),
          Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun z => f ((Lax323828.TupleFortification.lift G t).right z))
            (Finset.univ.expect fun w => f w)

soundness : ∀ {Z W A B : Type} [inst : Fintype Z] [inst_1 : Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] [Nonempty W] [Fintype A]
  (G : Lax323828.FortifiedSquaring.Game Z W A B) (t : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 t → ∀ (s : Real), G.Sound s → (Lax323828.TupleFortification.lift G t).Sound s

concepts.title: A tuple sampler with alphabet-independent mixing
concepts.description:
For an event S on t-tuples, plant a specified letter in a uniformly chosen
coordinate and sample the remaining coordinates independently. Let p_S(a)
be the probability of S under this experiment. Its mean is Pr[S], and
the square of its mean absolute deviation from Pr[S] is at most 1/t.

The alphabet size does not enter the bound. Using all tuples as questions
therefore gives a polynomial-size sampler for each fixed accuracy.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax323828.TupleAveraging

/-!
---
title: A tuple sampler with alphabet-independent mixing
type: theorem
---
For an event S on t-tuples, plant a specified letter in a uniformly chosen
coordinate and sample the remaining coordinates independently. Let p_S(a)
be the probability of S under this experiment. Its mean is Pr[S], and
the square of its mean absolute deviation from Pr[S] is at most 1/t.

The alphabet size does not enter the bound. Using all tuples as questions
therefore gives a polynomial-size sampler for each fixed accuracy.
-/

namespace Lax323828.TupleSampler

open scoped Classical

open FiniteProbability
open scoped BigOperators

/-- The value one on the event `S`, and zero outside it. -/
noncomputable def indicator {A : Type} (S : A → Prop) (a : A) : ℝ :=
  if S a then 1 else 0

/-- The average indicator after planting `a` at a uniformly chosen coordinate of a uniformly chosen tuple. -/
noncomputable def mass {A : Type} [Fintype A] (t : ℕ)
    (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) (a : A) : ℝ :=
  𝔼 i : Fin t, 𝔼 z : Fin t → A, indicator S (Function.update z i a)

axiom bounds {A : Type} [Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) (a : A) : 0 ≤ mass t S a ∧ mass t S a ≤ 1

axiom mean {A : Type} [Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) : (𝔼 a, mass t S a) = probability S

axiom mixing {A : Type} [Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) :
    (𝔼 a, |mass t S a - probability S|) ^ 2 ≤ 1 / (t : ℝ)

end Lax323828.TupleSampler

statements.signature:
bounds : ∀ {A : Type} [inst : Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 t →
    ∀ (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop) (a : A),
      And (Real.instLE.le 0 (Lax323828.TupleSampler.mass t S a)) (Real.instLE.le (Lax323828.TupleSampler.mass t S a) 1)

mean : ∀ {A : Type} [inst : Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 t →
    ∀ (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop),
      Eq (Finset.univ.expect fun a => Lax323828.TupleSampler.mass t S a) (Lax323828.FiniteProbability.probability S)

mixing : ∀ {A : Type} [inst : Fintype A] [Nonempty A] (t : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 t →
    ∀ (S : (Fin t → A) → Prop),
      Real.instLE.le
        (instHPow.hPow
          (Finset.univ.expect fun a =>
            abs (instHSub.hSub (Lax323828.TupleSampler.mass t S a) (Lax323828.FiniteProbability.probability S)))
          2)
        (instHDiv.hDiv 1 t.cast)

proofs.description:
Multiply the balanced zero-sum identity by a bounded function supported on S. All outside
coordinates have the same mean by a transposition; the inside sum is at
most |S| in absolute value.
Condition the independent-sign tail bound on the central binomial layer.

Absolute correlations are at most one, so increasing the support size can
only decrease their powers. Sum with nonnegative squared coefficients.

Factor the expectation coordinate by coordinate. A coordinate in just one
support contributes a zero mean; coordinates in both contribute the correlation.
Map a predicate to its set of true inputs, a bijection with n-element subsets.
The largest binomial layer has at least the average size of the N+1 layers.

Expand the square, interchange finite sums and expectations, and cancel
every pair of distinct supports using the balanced mixed-moment identity.
Apply bounded-support cancellation to the character on S.

Exponential Markov with parameter log 2. A Bernoulli variable has moment
1+p at this parameter, bounded by exp p; the independent moments multiply.

Union over every possible proof, then absorb the 2^m factor by choosing
the expected sample count at least m+2.

The uniform PCP and clique reduction give a polynomial-time fair-tape test
for every registered NP language. Rejection tapes certify its complement,
so complementary tests combine into a zero-error finite-tape algorithm.
The probability-preserving compiler implements it in the registered
probabilistic machine model with a worst-case polynomial clock. The reverse
inclusion is the proved registered containment ZPP ⊆ NP.

Combine the main clique-hardness implication with the imported inclusion
ZPP ⊆ BPP. Both statement dependencies are recorded by the archive.

Contraposition of the main clique-hardness implication. This proof retains
that implication as an explicit archive assumption.

Contrapose the BPP consequence; the imported classes have the same binary
language type, so no change of input encoding is involved.
Apply the proved decoding-set estimate at squared threshold τ²/ℓ.

Agreement forces the full Fourier sum to equal one. Split by degree and
coefficient size. Avoidance of the decoding set isolates the distinguished
label in each large support, making that term at most one third. Therefore
one of the two remaining terms is at least one third; use their proved tails.

Transpose the random query matrix into independent labels. Project onto
the satisfying words, preserving accepted answers and shrinking the decoding
set into the original decoding set intersected with those words. Every bad
accepting run then supplies a whole fiber of bad evaluation points.

Use the side-condition theorem with the constant true condition. Agreement
on that condition is equality of functions, so its extra checks are automatic.

Choose a coefficient threshold that decays slowly enough to keep the decoding
set small. Fixed moment and degree cutoffs make the pointwise error decay
faster than the requested exponential rate. Finally increase the word width
to control small fibers. The decoding set is independent of the side condition.
Apply soundness to a maximum clique and completeness to every proof.

Choose one accepting local view for each accepting random choice. All the
chosen views extend the given proof, so they are pairwise compatible.
An always-accepted proof attains all random choices, the universal upper bound.

Glue the compatible partial assignments in a clique, assigning false at
positions no view fixes. Distinct vertices have distinct random choices.
The universal acceptance bound also bounds its maximum.
Sum the per-choice bound on accepting local views.
Count the vertices separately for each random choice.

Fix a common answer separately for each second question. Randomly and
independently choose one of B+1 slots for every first question; every decoded
answer occupies a slot. Average over these global first-prover strategies
and fix one whose success is at least the average.
Count incidences first by points of the union and then by supports.

Choose two distinct covering positions for each point, take their union,
and enlarge this selection to the requested cardinality. This extracts
the double subcover used in Lemma 4.16.

The centered two-bit variable has all double-cover moments at least one.
Its lifted polynomial has degree at most 2l and second moment at most 3^l.
Apply the dimension-independent bounded-moment estimate.

Factor by coordinates. A coordinate with odd multiplicity has zero mean;
every even multiplicity contributes one.
A positive even multiplicity is at least two.

Expand the power as a sum over ordered tuples and apply the character
moment identity to each tuple.

Outside the union of CNA decoding failures, each accepting table has a
decoded assignment satisfying its side condition. Their projections agree
on all reference functions, so the many-table agreement bound applies.

The explicit finite FAF error decays faster than 2^(-20*l*l*s).
Acceptance above that target would therefore produce prover strategies
exceeding the stated game threshold, contradicting game soundness.

Sum over 2^q reference answer strings, and use the proved bound of 2^s
accepting side-condition patterns for each of the n tables.

Every factor is positive, so game soundness tending to zero can meet this
threshold for each fixed choice of the verifier parameters.

Filtering for consistency and merging views only decrease the number of
enumerated transcripts.

An extending proof supplies exactly the recorded reference and queried
table answers. Conversely, an actual accepting transcript is coherent
because every recorded bit comes from the same proof coordinate.
Encode the evaluation tables of perfect prover strategies as one proof.
The random-choice numbering is a bijection, and acceptance agrees pointwise.
Count one Boolean coordinate for every entry in every long-code table.

Multiply the independent choices of the reference question, extensions,
reference functions, and CNA functions.

Apply finite FAF soundness to the two table families decoded from each
global proof, and use the exact acceptance-probability identity.

Consistent satisfying assignments satisfy every side condition, and genuine
long codes pass every corresponding CNA test.

Noncommon questions contribute at most the finite FAF error. Therefore
common questions have mass at least acceptance minus that error. Apply the
proved rounding theorem to their decoded assignments.
Use the actual reference answers and the accepting pattern of each CNA test.

Choose every decoding set from the proved CNA soundness theorem with
epsilon one, then instantiate the finite extraction theorem. The thresholds
are independent of all tables, reference answers, projections and constraints.

Convexity bounds the exponential by its chord between -u and u. The mean
zero assumption cancels the linear part, leaving cosh(u) ≤ exp(u²/2).
Split a bounded moment into the part below q and the exceptional upper tail.
Every point of the tail contributes at least t^m to a nonnegative moment sum.
Each tail point contributes at least exp(u t) to a nonnegative exponential sum.
The indicator of a union is bounded by the sum of its member indicators.
Count the included event and divide by the size of the common sample space.
Restricting to a subset of mass at least 1/K inflates any event by at most K.
The cardinality of a union is at most the sum of the two cardinalities.
The absolute tail is the union of the upper tails for a and -a.
Factor the exponential moment over independent signs and bound each cosh factor.
Apply exponential Markov with u = t/v and optimize the quadratic exponent.

Fix the first random test and partition its successful answers by their
common projection. Each part is a rectangle in the second questions.
Apply fortification on each part and average; first-copy success is at
most the original soundness by fixing the second random test.
Apply Parseval and use that every sign has square one.

Parseval also bounds the energy of the real-valued averaged tables used
for side conditions, since every pointwise square is at most one.

Compare an arbitrary power with one plus a larger even power, then apply
dyadic hypercontractivity and the supplied second-moment bound.

The factors on the common coordinates square to one; the remaining support
is the symmetric difference.
The counting bound applies because Parseval gives total squared mass one.

A support meeting the positive threshold and containing a point is nonempty,
so its projected coefficient cannot vanish. The projection formula forces
the support to lie in U and identifies its coefficient with the original one.

Use linearity, the coefficient of the constant function, and the singleton
character shift.
Check the two possible signs of each Boolean value.

Iterate the fourth-moment inequality on powers of F. The degree bound grows
with the power; all resulting constants remain independent of dimension.

Expand the coefficients and interchange the two finite sums. The character
kernel vanishes away from x and equals the size of the cube at x.
Apply the polynomial estimate to the Fourier expansion and use Parseval.

Pair every input with its bitwise complement. For an even support its
character is unchanged, whereas the table value changes sign.

The sum factors coordinate by coordinate. A coordinate belonging to exactly
one support contributes zero, and otherwise every coordinate contributes two.
Specialize preservation of the uniform inner product to F with itself.

Fourier coefficients of a product are convolutions over symmetric difference.
A surviving support has cardinality at most the sum of the two degrees.

Expand F in characters. Averaging kills a character with any coordinate
outside U; orthogonality then extracts the remaining coefficient.
Use the triangle inequality for a finite sum and divide by the cube's cardinality.
Every term of the averaging sum has the same value.

Partition a single vector of fair bits into consecutive blocks using the
explicit product-index equivalence.

Every tuple of residues has at least floor(B/r)^N preimages. Apply this
lower bound to the complement event, then Bernoulli's inequality bounds
the mass lost in incomplete residue blocks by Nr/B.
Add the 1/12 sampling error to the graph construction's 1/4 bound.
Exponentiation of the seed space only multiplies its binary logarithm.

Binary interpretation is a bijection. The chosen power-of-two range is
at least 12Nr, making the total modulo error at most 1/12.

Choose l so that l*epsilon exceeds one, then choose the uniform CNA/FAF
parameters and a sampling multiplier. The local-test verifier has
free-bit/soundness ratio 1/l. Apply the proved randomized transfer, retaining
its explicit polynomial vertex bound.

The unary vertex count and delimiter occupy n+1 bits, and the n rows
of the adjacency matrix occupy n bits each.

Cancel unequal supports. For each fixed predicate, split correlation powers
at q, apply balanced concentration, and sum the squared coefficients.
Apply the even-moment tail inequality with exponent two.
Reorder the product by coordinates, then use independence of the labels.
The unique-occurrence coordinate contributes the mean of one balanced predicate.

The coordinate exponential moments multiply; optimize exponential Markov
with u = t/N for N independent centered summands in [-1,1].

Cancel each isolated distinguished label. The sum of coefficient magnitudes
is at most 1/δ because δ|c| ≤ c² on all retained supports.
Evaluation commutes with Boolean composition.
The map from an accepting pattern to its initial s answers is injective.

If no word produces the initial answer vector, the predicate recognizing
that vector composes to the constant false function, contradicting acceptance.
Functions agreeing on the side condition have equal values at a satisfying word.

The predicate recognizing the initial answer vector cannot vanish on every
satisfying word: step (3) would identify its accepted answer with false.

Each added query is constrained to equal a base query, so the initial
s answers still determine every answer in an accepting pattern.

Coordinate induction bounds the fourth moment by the squared Fourier energy
weighted by 3^|S|. Low degree bounds every surviving weight by 3^l.
Expand the majority-error indicator and factor the three independent averages.

The cubic error transformation is increasing on [0,1]. Exact rational bounds
for the three stages are 7/27, 17/100, and 1/12.

Split selections according to their number of distinct projected assignments.
Few distinct assignments are rare by the representative-table bound. For
each remaining selection, each random function has to be constant on its
image; take the union bound over all selections and then average over tables.

Choose one representative table for each selected value. Conditional on
these tables, all remaining independent tables must hit their union. Sum
over the at most 2^n possible representative sets.

All nonempty subcollections simultaneously have small correlation outside
an event controlled by a union bound. Factor the mixed moment over its
coordinate union and bound each factor by q on that good event.
Every answer involved in the acceptance equations is unchanged.
Acceptance checks the predicate defining a query and its Boolean complement.

The side condition identifies both a function and its complement with
queried functions. Such pairs are already consistent and are also kept.
Both members of a complementary pair are either kept or replaced by evaluation.
Transport cliques in both directions along the vertex numbering.
An encoded honest answer decodes to the original answer.
There are at least w Boolean words of length w; apply finite cardinality.

A winning encoded transcript has two valid encodings. Decoding and filling
missing answers arbitrarily gives total original strategies that still win
on each such transcript.
Give the first prover the two labels supplied by a satisfying assignment.

Complete partial answers arbitrarily. Every violated constraint forces a
rejection on at least one of its two endpoint tests. The dart involution
identifies this sampling rule with uniform vertex and extension sampling.
Take the union bound over all possible labels of a fiber.

Apply the independent bounded-variable tail bound to the negative centered
indicator of membership in the fiber.

The explicit gap forces every complete sampled instance to be accepted.
On a sound instance, acceptance forces the clique number into the bad
event already bounded by the sampling theorem.

Reuse the uniform PCP-to-clique gap reduction. Amplify the randomized
estimator's comparison, combine independent reduction and estimator tapes,
and accept only if two independent combined trials accept. The finite-tape
compiler realizes the resulting bounded-error test in the registered BPP model.

Contrapose the randomized implication through its concept statement so the
archive records the dependency in the proof network.

The expected sampled acceptance count is m+2. The multiplicative tail
bound applies simultaneously to all 2^m possible proofs.
Multiply the sample count by the accepting-view bound after repetition.
Compose the consistency-graph correspondence with invariance under numbering.

On low-optimum instances the estimator is at most a. On high-optimum
instances an output at most a would contradict the strict multiplicative gap.

Apply the ported Dinur gap amplifier, regularize with its fixed expander
family, and number the finite label, vertex, and dart-label spaces.
An empty output can occur only on satisfiable inputs and is replaced
by one unconstrained vertex of the same fixed degree.
Filtering for compatibility and merging cannot increase the product count.

Compatible views merge exactly when they are jointly extended. Conversely,
views accepted by a single global proof are automatically compatible.
The same perfect proof works in every repetition.

Transfer uniform seeds through their numbering equivalence and factor the
independent fixed-proof acceptance events.
Apply the exact probability identity to every fixed proof.

The certificate is a complete random tape. Its verifier parses the registered
pair encoding, checks the tape length, and simulates the registered procedure.
A globally accepting proof accepts every sample, including repeated seeds.

The sampled clique number is attained by one of the 2^m global proofs.
Apply the multiplicative tail bound simultaneously to all of them.
Each sample retains the base accepting-view bound.

The margin in the exponential dominates 4(m+2). The remaining exponent
is exactly the contribution of the graph-size approximation factor.

An integer strictly larger than the reciprocal of the positive margin
works for every input length.

The rounded binary logarithm loses at most a factor two. Raising its
exponential to the fixed power (t+f)c gives an explicit polynomial bound.
The extra queries force the averaging fiber to be constant at the queried value.

Cancel tuples that are not double covers. For small unions use the small
coefficient bound, and for large unions use mixed-predicate concentration.
Apply the finite even-moment tail inequality to the normalized Fourier sum.

Bound the union by the sum of support sizes, charge each support at least
ℓδ squared mass, and use the total squared-mass bound.

Extract a double subcover of size 2t, sum over the choices of its positions,
and bound each remaining support by the total coefficient mass on subsets
of its union. The extracted tuples are controlled by the double-cover bound.

The explicit registered-machine simulation supplies Cook–Levin, and the
fixed-alphabet soundness amplifier preserves a polynomial bound in input length.

Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to the event indicator and the centered sample mean.
The indicator's second moment is at most one.
The sampler mass is an average of indicators.
An independently sampled planted letter leaves the uniform tuple law unchanged.

Test the centered sampler density against its sign. The adjoint identity
turns this pairing into the restricted centered tuple average, whose
second moment has already been bounded independently of the alphabet.

Expand the centered second moment. Distinct coordinates have zero mixed
moment by independence; each diagonal variance is at most one.

Turning failure into rejection gives RP membership; the explicit random-tape
verifier then supplies an NP certificate.
